content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
zarrow is a Zig-native Apache Arrow library at `C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zarrow`. Branch `agent/zarrow-performance-zig-compat-adc67e` (commits a7b8fa7, 8aef605, 6ba9447) makes one source tree build on Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 and fixed the big performance bugs: geometric growth in `OwnedBuffer.resize` (`src/buffer.zig`), pairwise merge in `src/concat_array_refs.zig`, zero-copy IPC read (`StreamReader.initZeroCopy` in `src/ipc/stream_reader.zig`), plus a new `benchmarks/ipc_roundtrip_benchmark.zig`. Toolchains: Zig 0.17 is `zig` on PATH; Zig 0.16 is `C:\Users\cable\tools\zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0\zig.exe` (use `--cache-dir .zig-cache16`). Both `zig build test` runs must stay green (348 tests). Format with 0.16 `zig fmt` only (0.17 fmt rewrites `@intFromEnum` to `@backingInt`, which 0.16 rejects); local fmt --check noise is CRLF line endings, compare after `tr -d '\r'`. Parallel zstd compiles can flake with `SystemResources`; use `-j2` and retry. Run benchmarks one at a time with `zig build benchmark-<name>_benchmark -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`. API guides: `C:\Users\cable\.claude\skills\zig-0-16\SKILL.md` and `zig-0-17\SKILL.md`.

Task:
Two measured, deferred performance items in zarrow. Keep diffs minimal (ponytail style), no new abstractions, tests on both compilers.

1. Direct `take` gather kernel. `compute.datumTake` / `filter` in `src/compute/datum_permutation.zig` (~lines 197-221) build one length-1 `ArrayRef` slice per index and then concat them. After the pairwise-merge fix this is ~534 ns/row for 20k int32 rows; a direct gather (allocate the output buffers once, copy value + validity bit per index) should be ~5 ns/row. Implement it for primitive (all fixed-width) and boolean arrays first, fall back to the existing slice+concat path for other types. Add a `take` benchmark in the existing style (`benchmarks/*_benchmark.zig`, modes default/smoke/full/matrix/ci, register in `tools/benchmark_ci_check.py`, `tools/test_benchmark_ci_check.py`, `tools/benchmark_ci_thresholds.json`) and a test comparing the kernel's output to the fallback path for a nullable int32 and a boolean array with out-of-order and repeated indices.

2. Allocation trims in `record_batch_builder`: ~45% of its time is `page_allocator` syscalls for ~30 tiny allocations per iteration (105k ns/iter vs 60k with `smp_allocator`). Fold `BufferStorage` into the data allocation in `src/buffer.zig` (`toShared`, ~line 186) or otherwise cut per-finish allocations without changing the benchmark's allocator. Measure `zig build benchmark-record_batch_builder_benchmark -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` before and after; report min of 3 runs each.

Done when: `zig build test` and the 0.16 equivalent pass, both benchmarks run on both compilers, numbers reported in the commit message, committed on this branch.

Direct take gather kernel and fewer allocations per array finish

Performance (ReleaseFast, each benchmark run alone, default mode):
- take (new benchmarks/take_benchmark.zig: nullable int32, 200k rows,
  permuted indices with repeats): 17,560 -> 5.2 ns/row on Zig 0.17,
  6.1 ns/row on Zig 0.16. compute take/filter on array datums with a
  fixed-width or boolean layout now gather straight into output buffers
  (one values buffer, one validity buffer, one node) instead of building a
  length-1 ArrayRef per index and concatenating. Other layouts, chunked
  inputs and scalars keep the slice+concat path. datumFilter on array
  datums routes through datumFilterSelectionIndices + the same take.
- record_batch_builder (page_allocator, min of 3): 97,658 -> 90,232
  ns/iter on Zig 0.17; 92,504 ns/iter on Zig 0.16. Two allocation trims:
  * OwnedBuffer reserves ALIGNMENT bytes in front of the data for the
    BufferStorage header, so toShared no longer allocates a control block
    (buffer.zig). resize after toShared/deinit re-inits instead of growing
    the empty sentinel.
  * ArrayRef.fromOwnedInlineBuffers allocates the node and its buffers
    slice as one block; used by ArrayRef.slice, PrimitiveBuilder.finish,
    BooleanBuilder.finish and the take kernel. Other builders still use
    fromOwnedUnsafe with a separately allocated buffers slice.
  Remaining per-iteration allocations are the two builder value buffers,
  the RecordBatch column slices and the node blocks.

Tests: new compute test compares the gather kernel against the chunked
(slice+concat) path for a nullable int32 array with out-of-order and
repeated indices, checks boolean output bit by bit, and rejects an
out-of-range index. take registered in tools/benchmark_ci_check.py,
tools/test_benchmark_ci_check.py and tools/benchmark_ci_thresholds.json.
zig build test passes on Zig 0.16.0 and 0.17.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Commit 9598a31 on `agent/nostalgic-pasteur-afcbcf` (branch reset onto the perf branch tip 6ba9447 first, since it had no commits of its own). Nothing pushed.

**Numbers** (ReleaseFast, each benchmark alone, default mode):

| benchmark | before | after, Zig 0.17 | after, Zig 0.16 |

| take, 200k nullable int32, permuted+repeated indices | 17,560 ns/row | 5.2 ns/row | 6.1 ns/row |
| record_batch_builder, page_allocator, min of 3 | 97,658 ns/iter | 90,232 ns/iter | 92,504 ns/iter |

**What changed**

- [datum_permutation.zig](src/compute/datum_permutation.zig): `takeFixedWidthArray` gathers fixed-width and boolean array datums straight into one values buffer, one validity buffer and one node. Other layouts, chunked inputs and scalars keep slice+concat. `datumFilter` on array datums now goes through selection indices plus the same take.
- [buffer.zig](src/buffer.zig): the BufferStorage header lives in the first 64 bytes of the data allocation, so `toShared` allocates nothing. `resize` after `toShared` re-inits instead of growing the empty sentinel.
- [array_ref.zig](src/array/array_ref.zig): `fromOwnedInlineBuffers` allocates the node and its buffers slice as one block. Used by `slice`, the Int and Bool builder `finish`, and the take kernel.
- New [take_benchmark.zig](benchmarks/take_benchmark.zig), registered in the three CI tool files. New test compares the kernel to the chunked path for nullable int32, checks bool output bit by bit, rejects an out-of-range index.
- Both `zig build test` runs pass; python CI checker tests pass.

**Caveat on item 2:** record_batch_builder run-to-run noise is 90k to 130k ns/iter, so the gain is about 8%, not the 45% the profile suggested. The remaining allocations per iteration are the two builder value buffers (page-sized), the RecordBatch column slices, and four node blocks. Full notes are in the shared notes folder as `take-kernel-and-alloc-trims.md`.

Skipped: other builders still allocate a separate buffers slice. Add `fromOwnedInlineBuffers` to them when a builder-heavy benchmark shows it matters.
